Name: Steven Garry
Notes:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am currently looking for an experienced Director of Photography and cinematic drone operator to collaborate on a short teaser for my award-winning science-fiction screenplay, [i]Gulf of Aden[/i].
The teaser will be filmed across several Liverpool locations, including Moorfields Station, the city centre, an interior period setting and the waterfront. It combines a runner’s journey through Liverpool with a low-level drone movement across enclosed dock water and out towards the Mersey, intercut with a tense dialogue scene involving senior political and financial figures.
The production is microbudget, but the creative ambition and potential stakes are considerable. Approximately half of the teaser cast has already been established, and discussions regarding locations and permissions are under way.
The immediate requirement is for:
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left]A Director of Photography or highly experienced camera operator capable of helping achieve a cinematic, controlled visual style using a relatively small crew.[/li][li indent=0 align=left]A qualified and insured drone operator with strong cinematic flying experience, particularly low-level movement over water, controlled acceleration, reflection shots and gradual skyline reveals.[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Ideally, someone interested in working collaboratively with me as the writer and director, rather than simply providing a standard corporate video service.[/li][/ul][/ml]The teaser is being produced for submission to the Future Vision XPRIZE Moonshots competition, associated with Google and Revenge Media. The competition is seeking optimistic and ambitious science-fiction concepts with the potential to influence how audiences imagine the future.
Following any success generated by the teaser, the screenplay or the Moonshots competition, I would also be interested in discussing a possible longer-term creative collaboration.
[h3]Project information[/h3]
[b]Gulf of Aden – Official Project Website[/b]
[url=https://gulf-of-aden-movie.netlify.app/]https://gulf-of-aden-movie.netlify.app[/url]
[b]Moonshots Competition – Future Vision XPRIZE[/b]
[url=https://futurevisionxprize.com/]https://futurevisionxprize.com[/url]
[i]Gulf of Aden[/i] is an ambitious, independently developed science-fiction feature project. The Liverpool shoot will create a short cinematic teaser for submission to the Future Vision XPRIZE Moonshots competition.
The teaser is not intended to summarise the entire feature. It is designed to immerse the audience in the emotional and philosophical language of the film before revealing its wider narrative. Its central idea is human alignment: three apparently separate movements—a lone runner crossing Liverpool, a camera journey across the dock waters towards the Mersey, and a discussion unfolding inside a private suite—gradually become one.
I have prepared a detailed Director’s Teaser Treatment explaining the visual structure, locations, camera movement, drone sequence and dramatic intention. I would be happy to provide this, along with the relevant screenplay scene and supporting visual references, to suitable filmmakers.
I would be grateful if you could recommend any Liverpool or North West-based cinematographers, camera operators, drone pilots or small production teams who may be suited to this type of ambitious independent film project.
Kind regards,
Steven James Garry
Writer and Director
[i]Gulf of Aden[/i]

Paradisus Social Campaign Shoot 


BRIEF 


What we need to produce
A social-first content and lifestyle photography shoot at Paradisus Gran Canaria, designed to capture the full breadth of the Paradisus family offering. Delivered through a lean production model with a compact crew and lightweight equipment package, the shoot remains agile and low impact while maximising content output across multiple locations and experiences.
The resulting content will serve as a core brand asset for the UK and US markets, with additional application across commercial, editorial and social channels.


Project Objectives
The primary campaign message is the perfect family holiday. Wellness is a hygiene factor -intrinsic to the brand experience and present in the visual world, but not the hero of the story.
Establish the Paradisus family offering — across the full brand portfolio — as the reference in luxury all-inclusive family holidays.
Showcase everything that makes Paradisus the ideal choice for families: KIDSDOM, YOUR WAY, exclusive family and adults-only spaces, gastronomy designed for all ages, and premium rooms.
Generate a bank of premium lifestyle content for organic social media deployment across Instagram and TikTok, with additional use for commercial support materials.
Reinforce Wellness. Designed by Destination as the brand USP through visual storytelling rooted in family fun, Gran Canaria's landscape, light, culture, and gastronomy, without making wellness the explicit campaign message.
This shoot adopts a social-first production model, combining a streamlined crew structure with portable equipment to maximise content output while maintaining a discreet presence on site.

Target audience: 

Primary market: United Kingdom & US. Secondary: broader European markets (ES, FR, DE).
Travel motivators:
Stress-free, premium family holidays where everything is taken care of
Authentic connection with the destination — not just the pool
Experiences designed for every member of the family simultaneously
A resort that feels like a reward — for parents as much as for children


Psychographic profile:
Affluent families, 35–50 years old, with children and/or teenagers
They seek quality and curation — they recognize the difference between premium and merely expensive
Active on Instagram; increasingly using TikTok for travel inspiration
Aspire to holidays that balance family togetherness with genuine personal restoration
Profiles:
Relief Seekers — parents who need to truly switch off and trust that everything is handled
Memory Makers — families for whom the holiday is about shared experiences and emotional connection
Joy Rejuvenators — travelers who return home feeling restored, not just rested
Mandatory creative requirements:
Warm, natural light — Gran Canaria's Atlantic quality of light should be a signature of the shoot
Real moments over posed perfection — lifestyle, not catalogue
Diversity of family configurations welcome — the brief is not prescriptive about family makeup
Children should appear as protagonists in their own right, not only as kids being supervised by their parents
Children and teenagers should feel authentic — genuinely engaged, not performing for camera
The resort's architecture, landscaping and design should feature as a character in the content
Talent:


Casting should resonate with the UK&US market — aspirational but accessible, reflecting the warmth and diversity of contemporary British family life.


Campaign deliverables:


1 overarching creative concept for video, to be presented by ANAGRAM prior to production. All video content must be adapted for both Instagram Reels and TikTok — footage may be shared, but edit, pacing and tone must be differentiated by platform.
Instagram Reels: aspirational, polished, brand-forward. TikTok: spontaneous, energetic, culturally native.

Zara Kids (In general, specifically Mommy & Me collaboration) the way premium childrenswear brands shoot family lifestyle: warm, considered, modern. The family as a style unit, not a demographic.
Bobo Choses — independent Spanish childrenswear brand with a strong visual world: playful, artistic, never saccharine. A reference for how to show childhood with sophistication and without cliché.
These references reflect a consistent direction: elevated but not cold, family-focused but not folksy, aspirational without being alienated to the UK market.

Name: Anastasia Mcvicker
Notes:
Need videos for a product launch, including the founder why, product videos and product how-to's. Suggested scenes below:

ENCHANTABLY
Founder Intro Reels — Videographer Brief
Six films across three sections · Founder: Anastasia · Vertical 9:16 · Instagram-first

WHAT WE’RE SELLING, IN ONE LINE
Enchantably makes personalized children’s books where the child is the hero of the story. This brief covers six films across three sections: the founder’s “why” (Section 1, Films 1–4), the product’s tactile magic (Section 2, Film 5), and the path to ordering one (Section 3, Film 6). Together they form a complete channel launch — emotional anchors that earn trust, a product film that conveys what’s actually being sold, and an instructional film that never feels instructional. None of them should feel like ads.
NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES (PLEASE READ FIRST)
NO children’s faces, ever. The founder’s two sons appear only as silhouettes, hands, or off-camera audio. This is a hard safety requirement, not a stylistic preference. When in doubt, frame tighter or shoot from behind.
Warm, natural light throughout. Window light preferred. No cool or blue tones — those read as “tech,” and these films are about the opposite of tech. (Exception: Film 3 hook is intentionally lit only by laptop glow — see Film 3.)
Burn-in subtitles on all four films. Default viewing is sound-off.
Slow, contemplative pacing on Films 1–3. Cut just AFTER the beat, not on it. Think perfume ad, not creator reel. Film 4 is slightly snappier (listicle structure) but still warmer than typical TikTok content.
Everything shot vertical 9:16 from the start. No horizontal “for safety.”
Never reference “AI” in voiceover or text overlays in any film. The technology is how the books are made, not what they are.


SECTION 1
About the Founder
Four films that earn the audience’s trust before anything is sold.

FILM 1
“The Kid I Used to Be”
The deeper, more personal film — the anchor of the trio. The founder grew up on Soviet-era children’s tales and sensed, even as a small child, that their lessons were wrong for her. This is the film that earns the audience’s trust. Post this one first; it gets pinned to the profile.


SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:05  HOOK
VISUAL  Close-up of founder’s hands holding the worn Soviet book. Cyrillic on the cover. Soft window light, phone slightly above looking down.
V/O  “I’m not just building this for my kids. I’m building it for the kid I used to be.”
TEXT  the kid i used to be (small, lowercase, serif)
0:05–0:16  THE STORIES
VISUAL  Slow page turns landing on a recognizable illustration for each tale as it is named. If the book lacks them, intercut three staged illustration close-ups (warm, faded).
V/O  “Kolobok runs off to see the world — and gets eaten. Snegurochka melts the first time she feels love. Morozko rewards the silent daughter and freezes the bold one.”
NOTE  ~3.5 sec per tale. Sequence them — never show all three at once. Half-beat pause between each tale and its fate.
0:16–0:24  THE PATTERN
VISUAL  Cut to founder on camera. Medium close-up, soft light, looking directly at lens. The Soviet book set down beside her.
V/O  “I was five when I started to notice. The curious got punished. The brave girls only mattered when they were saving someone else. I didn’t have the words for it then. But I felt it.”
NOTE  Delivery is plain, almost flat. The power is in the understatement.
0:24–0:32  THE BUILD
VISUAL  Couch silhouette — two small shapes piled on her lap, screen glow, soft giggling. Then close-up of an Enchantably book opening, the child’s name visible.
V/O  “My boys are growing up differently. In their books, they are the hero from page one. Curious. Brave. Worth the whole story. The stories teach them valuable lessons about life in 2020’s and beyond. I built Enchantably because I couldn’t find the books I wanted them to have — and I knew exactly what those books needed to say.”
0:32–0:40  THE PAYOFF
VISUAL  Founder holding the old Soviet book in one hand, the Enchantably book in the other. Looks at both, then sets them side by side on the table.
ON CAM  “I’m Ana. I made Enchantably for my boys. And for every kid who deserves to be the hero of their own story — especially the ones who already know it, even before they have the words.”
TEXT  Enchantably — Stories where every child is the hero. (final card)

MUSIC & GRADE
Solo piano, melancholic but not sad (Ólafur Arnalds / Joep Beving / Nils Frahm lane, royalty-free). Always under the voice, never over it. Warm color grade, slight film grain.
FILM 2
“The Love Letter on the Shelf”
The universal companion to Film 1. Where Film 1 is the founder’s specific story, this one is the truth it points to: most things we buy our kids disappear; a personalized book stays. Post 7–10 days after Film 1.


SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:04  HOOK
VISUAL  Wide shot, slow gentle push-in on a lived-in bookshelf in soft natural light. Worn spines, stuffed animals, a framed photo angled away.
TEXT  “In 20 years, your kid won’t remember most of the things you buy them.” (large, centered, serif)
AUDIO  Soft, slow piano. No voiceover yet — let the text breathe the full 4 seconds.
0:04–0:09  THE WEIGHT
VISUAL  Slow montage across “the stuff”: plastic toy half-buried in a bin, tablet face-down on a coffee table, outgrown tee folded on a chair, worn small sneakers by the door.
V/O  “The toys. The gadgets. The clothes they grew out of in a season. Most of it ends up in a donation bag.”
0:09–0:16  THE TURN
VISUAL  Slow cut to a single hardcover book on a shelf, child’s name on the spine (sample name, or angled partial). Light catches it.
V/O  “But there’s one thing they’ll still pull off the shelf when they’re thirty. The book on the shelf with their name on it. The one where they were the hero. The one you made for them.”
0:16–0:23  FOUNDER REVEAL
VISUAL  Cut to founder — medium close-up, soft window light, holding the Enchantably book in her lap, looking down then up at the lens. Contemplative, not posed.
ON CAM  “I’m Ana. I’m a mom of two boys. I made Enchantably to be a love letter they can hold — written before they were old enough to read it. Before the world got a chance to tell them who they were supposed to be.”
NOTE  Three landings, each firmer than the last. Second sentence slower and gentler; third sentence more certain (not louder).
0:23–0:30  THE PAYOFF
VISUAL  Back to the bookshelf. A small silhouetted hand (fingers only) slides the Enchantably book off the shelf. Cut to the book opening in small hands on a couch — pages turning, name catching the light.
V/O  “Give them the one thing that never ends up in the donation bag.”
TEXT  Enchantably — The book that stays on the shelf. (final card)
NOTE  Closing line is a deliberate callback to the “donation bag” in the opening — it loops the film shut.

MUSIC & GRADE
Warmer than Film 1 — acoustic fingerpicking or a warm-toned piano (Sleeping at Last instrumental lane). Same warm grade so the films feel like a set.
FILM 3
“The Books I Cry Every Time I Make”
The bravest film of the three. About Safety Magic — the part of Enchantably where the founder generates personalized stories that teach kids critical safety rules (fire, getting lost, stranger situations, water, road, home alone). She genuinely cries when making these. The film honors that truth and lets it do the persuasion. Post 7–10 days after Film 2.




SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:08  HOOK
VISUAL  Dark room, late night. Tight close-up of a laptop screen showing the Enchantably interface mid-generation (blur sensitive UI). A hand resting on the trackpad. The hand lifts away. The room is silent except for the laptop fan.
V/O  “I’m building a story about my son getting lost in a grocery store. I have to stop. Breathe. I cry every time I make these books.”
LIGHTING  EXCEPTION TO THE WARM-LIGHT RULE. This scene is lit ONLY by the laptop glow. The coolness is intentional — it isolates the founder in the moment of resistance.
0:08–0:20  THE WHY
VISUAL  Slow reveal of Safety Magic illustrations rendering or appearing on screen — a small figure alone in a crowd, an interior with a smoke alarm, a doorway with an unfamiliar adult silhouette. Restrained. No more than 2 seconds per image.
V/O  “Every Safety Magic story puts my kids — by name, in illustrations that look like them — into a dangerous situation. Lost. A fire at 2am. A stranger at the door. The instinct is to close the laptop and build something easier.”
NOTE  Pacing slower than Films 1 and 2. The images need to feel heavy. Half-beat pauses between “Lost.” “A fire at 2am.” “A stranger at the door.”
0:20–0:28  THE TURN
VISUAL  Cut to founder on camera. Medium close-up. Soft natural light (we are out of the laptop-glow scene now — it is morning, or a different day). Composed, but with the weight of someone who has done this work and felt it. Eyes may be slightly red.
ON CAM  “But the resistance is exactly the reason to keep building. If even I want to look away — every parent is looking away. And their kids don’t have the rehearsal.”
0:28–0:36  THE BUILD
VISUAL  Couch silhouette — different from Films 1 and 2. QUIETER. Two small shapes piled on her lap, screen glow, NO laughter this time. A small finger pointing at the screen. A stillness. Then a close-up of a Safety Magic book open on a child’s lap (silhouetted).
V/O  “A 5-year-old who hears the rules on Tuesday isn’t the same kid who wakes up to a smoke alarm at 2am. Stories aren’t information. They’re rehearsal.”
NOTE  Critical: this couch shot must feel different from the one in Films 1 and 2. Same setup, different energy. The silence carries it.
0:36–0:43  THE PAYOFF
VISUAL  Hold on the Safety Magic book in small hands. Quiet room.
OFF-CAM  (small voice, real, not theatrical) “Mom, what if there’s a fire on the second floor?”
NOTE  Let this question land. Hold 1.5–2 seconds of silence after the question before cutting back to founder. This is the emotional payoff of the entire film.
ON CAM  (softly, after the silence) “These aren’t my kids’ favorite books. They’re the books they think about. That question is the whole point. I’m Ana. And I’ll keep making these until every kid has one.”
TEXT  Safety Magic by Enchantably — Stories that prepare them without scaring them. (final card)

MUSIC & GRADE
Sparser than Films 1 and 2. A single piano note at a time, or ambient/drone with no melody. Avoid anything that tries to manipulate emotion — the emotion is already there. Music should be a frame, not a force. Possible references: Max Richter (“On the Nature of Daylight” restraint), Hildur Guðnadóttir, or simply room tone with very minimal piano. Same warm grade as Films 1 and 2 (except the laptop-glow opening, which stays cool). Burn-in subtitles essential.



FILM 4
“Things My Friends Don’t Know I Do at Night”
The lightest film of the four — and the most viral-shaped. Listicle structure, voyeuristic hook, deadpan humor that turns warm at the end. This is the discovery vehicle: the film designed to bring new followers in to the deeper founder anchors. Posting cadence is flexible (see note below).




SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:03  HOOK
VISUAL  Overhead shot of founder’s hands typing on a laptop at the kitchen table. Soft warm lamp light. A mug of tea. The house is dark and quiet around her.
TEXT  “Things my mom-friends don’t know I do after the boys go to bed…” (large, centered, serif, lingers full 3 sec)
AUDIO  Soft music begins. NO voiceover yet — let the text breathe. Music should be lighter than Films 1–3 (warm acoustic fingerpicking lane).
0:03–0:08  ITEM 1
VISUAL  Same overhead. Laptop screen visible — a children’s book draft or design tool (blur sensitive UI). Hands continue typing or sliding the laptop closer.
TEXT  1. Quietly run a kids’ book company from this kitchen table
V/O  (dry, conspiratorial, slight smile) “Number one — I’m quietly running a kids’ book company from this exact spot.”
0:08–0:14  ITEM 2
VISUAL  Close-up of founder — mouth/jawline only, or hands gesturing at the screen. A slight head shake at whatever she’s reading. A small wry smile. Maybe a sip of tea.
TEXT  2. Argue out loud about whether dragons should be friendly
V/O  (amused, deadpan) “Number two — I argue with myself out loud about whether the dragon should be sad or joyful. He shouldn’t always be.”
NOTE  The punchline is “He shouldn’t always be.” Land it flat — the humor is in the matter-of-factness.
0:14–0:22  ITEM 3 — THE TONAL SHIFT
VISUAL  Switch to a different time of day — softer evening light. Wide shot from behind/side. The silhouette of founder on a couch, two small shapes piled on her lap, laptop screen glowing on all three of them. Soft giggles.
TEXT  3. Test every story with the world’s harshest critics
V/O  (tone now warm, sincere) “Number three — I don’t keep any story until both my boys climb on my lap, read it on my screen, and connect with the story.”
NOTE  This is the pivot. The joke ends here and the real reason begins. Same listicle structure, completely different emotional register.
0:22–0:28  BUILD TO PAYOFF
VISUAL  Close-up of a printed Enchantably book on the kitchen table or being held in small hands. Real, hardcover, finished.
V/O  (warm, quiet) “The ones they say ‘I love it a million’ — those are the story arcs we publish.”
0:28–0:32  PAYOFF
VISUAL  Slow push-in on a small stack of finished Enchantably books, or on the open book in small hands.
OFF-CAM  (small voice, real, recorded separately) “Mom, can we read the million one again?”
V/O  “I’m Ana. I’m building Enchantably.”
TEXT  Enchantably — The book your kid says ‘I love it a million.’ (final card)
NOTE  “I love it a million” is the recurring brand quotable across the channel — capture this audio cleanly and use it as a hook in future content.

MUSIC & GRADE
Lighter than Films 1–3 — warm acoustic fingerpicking or a soft, playful piano (think the brighter end of the Sleeping at Last instrumental lane). Still warm-toned, still under the voice, but with a touch more lift than the contemplative anchors. Same warm color grade as the other films so the channel reads as a coherent set.


SECTION 2
About the Product
One film that conveys what the book actually is — without ever explaining it.

FILM 5
“The Book About Everything THEY Love”
The product film. We watch a child’s entire inner world — the people, places, dreams, friends, language — pour into one book, and then watch the child read themselves as the hero of all of it. Almost no voiceover. Sound design, music, text overlays, and tactile shots do the work. This is closer to a perfume commercial than a creator reel.




SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:03  COLD OPEN
VISUAL  Overhead on a child’s bedroom floor in warm afternoon light. A scatter of objects that compose a childhood: small toy plane, tiny globe, crayon drawing of a family, stuffed friend, play stethoscope or astronaut helmet. A small hand (silhouette only) reaches in.
TEXT  Everything he loves —
AUDIO  Soft, warm music begins (music-box adjacent). No voiceover.
0:03–0:07  THE WISH
VISUAL  Quick satisfying close-ups of each object. Each one paired with a word appearing on an Enchantably screen with a faint glow: stuffed animal → “his best friend”; globe → “Paris”; helmet → “an astronaut”; family drawing → names of the family members.
AUDIO  Soft chime per word appearance. Music builds gently.
NOTE  4–5 quick match cuts in 4 seconds. Words appear as if magicked into existence, not typed mechanically — use a soft fade-in, not a typewriter effect.
0:07–0:12  THE REVEAL
VISUAL  Match cuts: each real object dissolves into its illustrated self inside a book spread. The crayon family drawing becomes an illustrated family page. The globe becomes a page with the child in front of the Eiffel Tower. The helmet becomes the child as an astronaut. The stuffed friend becomes their illustrated companion.
AUDIO  Chime per transition. Music swells.
NOTE  THIS IS THE MONEY SHOT OF THE ENTIRE FILM. Spend extra post-production time getting these transitions seamless. The visual surprise of “my child’s actual drawing became an illustration in their book” is the marketing moment.
0:12–0:16  THE LANGUAGE BEAT
VISUAL  Hold on a page of text inside the book. The text writes itself in one language, then gently flips/transforms into another. Same sentence, two languages.
TEXT  in the language you speak — or want them to.
AUDIO  Soft voice reads the sentence in English; second voice (or same voice) reads it in a second language (heritage / target). Let the second reading complete fully.
NOTE  Hold this beat LONGER than the others. For bilingual and immigrant households, this is the buy moment. Founder may want to record her own voice in Russian here for personal authenticity — her call.
0:16–0:21  SCREEN TO SHELF
VISUAL  Hard cut to the physical product. A hand slides the printed hardcover Enchantably book out of its shipping box. Tactile close-ups of cover, spine, the weight of the book in two hands.
AUDIO  Chime fades. Music continues. Subtle paper/cardboard sound design — the book leaving the box has a satisfying tactile sound.
NOTE  The visual contrast between digital glow (previous beats) and physical paper (this beat) is the whole point. Ground it. The product is real.
0:21–0:30  THE PAYOFF
VISUAL  Child’s lap, soft bedtime light. Small hands turning pages slowly. We see the spreads from earlier — illustrated as astronaut, in Paris, with best friend, with family — one after another. Page after page is his entire world.
TEXT  He’s the hero of all of it.
AUDIO  Music swells to warmest point. Pages turning. Maybe a small contented sound from the child (off-mic).
NOTE  Don’t rush the page turns. Each spread should land. This is the emotional payoff.
0:30–0:34  CLOSE
VISUAL  Book closes. Hugged to chest (back of head only — silhouette). A soft sparkle or warmth fades out.
TEXT  Make theirs at enchantably.com (final card)
AUDIO  Music resolves. Single final chime.

MUSIC & GRADE
Whimsical and warm — music-box adjacent. Reference lane: Joe Hisaishi at his most tender, Yann Tiersen’s lighter moments, Alexandre Desplat’s children’s film scores. Sound design is doing more work in this film than any other; budget proper sound-mixing time. Same warm color grade as the other films. Burn-in subtitles essential.


SECTION 3
How to Use It
One film that converts — instructional content that never announces itself as instructional.

FILM 6
“The Book That Wrote Itself”
The how-to film, filmed as if a spell is being cast. The instructional content (name your hero, add the people they love, choose the adventure, add a photo, pick a format) is fully present — but it reads as ritual, not as a UI walkthrough. The setup is a stuffed animal alone on a windowsill. The payoff is that same stuffie illustrated inside the printed book a child is reading. The arc between those two shots is the entire film.




SCRIPT & SHOT-BY-SHOT
0:00–0:05  THE INVITATION
VISUAL  A stuffed animal sits alone on a windowsill in soft afternoon light. Slightly lonely framing — a lot of negative space around the toy. Camera pushes in slowly.
AUDIO (off-cam)  A parent’s voice, off-camera, soft and intimate: “Want to go on an adventure?”
MUSIC  Quiet. Single piano note. Almost silence.
NOTE  The whisper is the emotional setup of the entire film. Record it as if you are actually whispering to a teddy bear, not delivering a marketing line.
0:05–0:11  FIRST INPUT — WHO IS THE HERO?
VISUAL  Cut to a laptop/iPad screen, filmed close, intimate, slightly warm. The Enchantably interface is visible but the focus is on a finger typing a name. The actual UI fields can be visible — just shoot them like an incantation, not a demo.
TEXT  1. Name your hero (small, subtle, lower-third)
AUDIO  Soft chime as the name appears. A flicker of illustration blooms in a preview area.
0:11–0:16  THE COMPANIONS
VISUAL  More typing. The toy’s name (which we will later see illustrated). A sibling’s name. A best friend’s name. Each appears with a chime and a small illustrated flicker.
TEXT  2. Add the people they love
AUDIO  Chime per name. Music begins to build.
0:16–0:21  THE WORLD
VISUAL  A hand scrolls through story themes — the actual Enchantably UI showing visual options (blur any sensitive copy). The finger pauses, taps a story. The screen blooms with that world’s illustration.
TEXT  3. Choose their adventure
AUDIO  Chime. Music swells slightly.
0:21–0:26  THE PHOTO
VISUAL  A hand slides a small photo (or a child’s drawing) toward the device, or taps to upload. The screen accepts it. An illustration begins to render that resembles the real object — ideally we briefly see a likeness emerge.
TEXT  4. Add a face, a drawing, a memory
AUDIO  Chime. Subtle render sound.
0:26–0:31  MAKE IT REAL
VISUAL  A hand hovers between format options (digital preview, hardcover, paperback). Settles on hardcover. Tap.
TEXT  5. Make it real
AUDIO  Final chime. Music begins to resolve.
0:31–0:38  THE ARRIVAL
VISUAL  Cut: a shipping box arriving on a doorstep (or being lifted off a counter). Small hands opening it. The hardcover book emerging. Then: child holding the book, opening it, and finding their stuffie illustrated inside. CRITICAL match-cut moment with the windowsill stuffie.
AUDIO (off-cam)  Music swells to warmth. A small voice, this time the child’s: “Hi, friend.”
NOTE  The stuffie-on-windowsill ↔ illustrated-stuffie-in-book match is the emotional payoff of the entire film. Compose the framing so the visual rhyme is unmistakable. Same animal, same colors, same proportions.
0:38–0:42  CLOSE
VISUAL  Book closes. Child hugs the book to their chest (back of head silhouette only). Light fades.
TEXT  Start their story at enchantably.com (final card)
AUDIO  Music resolves. Final chime, slightly different from Film 5’s closing chime so the two films aren’t mistaken for each other.

MUSIC & GRADE
Same music lane as Film 5 (whimsical, music-box adjacent) but sparser and more ritualistic. Each chime needs to land cleanly — they are the punctuation of the spell. Same warm color grade as the rest of the channel. Burn-in subtitles essential.


ONE NOTE ON EFFICIENCY
Six films sounds like a lot — but they all draw from a small, shared pool of assets. Plan three sessions. Session A (Solo founder, ~75 min): founder on camera for Films 1–4 + artifact shots (Soviet book, family photo, bookshelf, “the stuff” montage) + the late-night kitchen workspace for Film 3 + UI capture for Film 6. Session B (Couch silhouette with the boys, ~20 min): capture three emotional registers — laughter (Films 1, 2, 4), quiet/alert stillness (Film 3), and the bedtime page-turn intimacy (Films 5, 6 payoff). Session C (Product and objects, ~45 min): the scatter of “world ingredients” for Film 5’s cold open, the match-cut spreads from the real book, the stuffie-on-windowsill setup for Film 6, the shipping-box unboxing shots. Three pieces of off-camera audio are critical across the channel: “Mom, what if there’s a fire on the second floor?” (Film 3), “Mom, can we read the million one again?” (Film 4), and “Hi, friend” (Film 6). Plus the recurring brand quotable “I love it a million.” Record all of these cleanly during Session B with multiple takes.

[h2]What we need[/h2]
We're looking for a videographer with strong creative instincts to capture Conveo's presence at Cannes Lions 2026. This isn't a "follow the team around and press record" brief. We need someone who can read a room, find the moment before it happens, and come back with footage that tells a story without a narrator explaining it.
You'll be working largely independently. We'll share the week's schedule and give you context on what's happening and when, but we expect you to make editorial calls. If you see something worth filming, film it. If something on the schedule isn't worth filming, skip it and find something that is.

[h2]What Conveo is doing at Cannes[/h2]
[b]Sunday 21 June — Yacht event (pre-Lions)[/b] An invite-only VIP cocktail event on a yacht anchored off the Croisette. Around 40 senior marketing and insights leaders. The setting, the guest calibre, and the concept are all strong visually. This is the single most important filming moment of the week.
[b]Monday to Friday — Casa Conveo[/b] A private villa-style venue off the Croisette running all week as a premium workspace and hosted event space. Four programmed events: a Monday reception, Tuesday sundown cocktails, Wednesday marquee night, and Thursday advisory lunch. Daily ambient activity throughout.
[b]Monday + Tuesday — Panels at the Palais[/b] Conveo moderates two official panels at the Insights Summit and Executive Retreat. Strong stage moments, good speaker calibre.
[b]Around the festival — Conveo's ad campaign[/b] We've placed content across seven screens at Cannes: the Palais Big Screen, Terrace Totems, Croisette Garden Screens, Hotel Splendid facade, Palais Harbour screen, JCDecaux city screens (37 locations), and the Palais Basement. Pure typographic creative. Worth capturing in context — the ads next to real festival foot traffic, delegates stopping to read, the Croisette dual-screen contrast. These are strong visual moments if caught right.

[h2]Deliverables[/h2]
[b]Priority outputs:[/b]
[ml][ol][li indent=0 align=left][b]Yacht event film[/b] — 60 to 90 seconds. The concept, the setting, the people, the energy. Should feel premium and effortless, not produced. The kind of thing you'd watch twice.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Casa Conveo week film[/b] — 90 to 120 seconds. The space, the conversations, the moments between moments. Not a highlight reel with music over talking heads. The texture of the week.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Ads in context[/b] — 15 to 30 seconds of clean, cinematic shots of Conveo's campaign running in the wild. Screens at night. Delegates walking past. Close-up of copy. Wide of the Croisette. This should feel editorial, not like a product demo.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Short-form social cuts[/b] — 3 to 5 clips of 15 to 30 seconds each, vertical (9:16) for social. Grab-and-go moments: a great line from a panel, a wide of the yacht at golden hour, the bar reveal, a conversation in the Casa Conveo garden.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]B-roll library[/b] — Raw, well-exposed, stable footage of: the Croisette, screens, crowd energy, Casa Conveo interiors and exteriors, panel moments, evening events. Clean enough to cut into future brand content.[/li][/ol][/ml][h2]What good looks like[/h2]
[b]Tone:[/b] Intelligent, warm, a little cinematic. Premium without being cold. The kind of coverage that makes people who weren't there wish they were, without feeling like an advertisement.
[b]What to look for:[/b]
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left]The moment someone reads the ad on the Croisette and reacts[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Real conversations, not posed interviews[/li][li indent=0 align=left]The physical contrast between the festival noise and the calm of Casa Conveo[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Guests on the yacht at golden hour[/li][li indent=0 align=left]The bar reveal concept (we'll brief you specifically on this before Sunday)[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Speakers in full flow, not just standing at a podium[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Small details: the insight cards, the sailor caps mid-evening, the screen glow at night[/li][/ul][/ml][b]What to avoid:[/b]
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left]Talking-head testimonials (we'll handle those separately if needed)[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Wide shots of empty rooms[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Anything that looks like a conference recap video[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Branding forced into shot — if it appears naturally, great; don't engineer it[/li][/ul][/ml]
